rows.evidence: evals/cases/electron-change.md, main.js: async before-quit listener neither receives the event nor synchronously prevents default quit. Electron does not await a returned listener Promise. Promise.race([flushLedger(), delay(1000)]) leaves the losing flush running, then tearDownDatabase() is called; a rejected flush is also unhandled in the snippet.
rows.next_step: Use one guarded, shared shutdown sequence that synchronously intercepts cancellable local quit requests and explicitly completes quit afterwards. Separate a failed cancellable checkpoint from irreversible teardown; actually cancel or join unfinished writes before database disposal, retain writer ownership, and define a terminal recovery path. Test repeated quit, slow/rejected flush, disposal beyond the deadline and window-close versus application-quit; test OS session end separately.
rows.reason: Code defect: the one-second wait does not own the exit lifecycle or terminate its outstanding operation. Returning to usable UI after irreversible disposal would also be unsafe.

device_plan.device: Physical supported Windows laptop/desktop with two monitors or dock, fractional/high mixed scaling and a standard-user account
device_plan.scenario: Install the final supported-CPU MSI. Save bounds on the non-primary display with a draft and dialog open; undock/remove that display, change taskbar work area, close/relaunch, then reconnect and move between scales. Repeat snap/maximize/restore and sleep/wake during a pending write.
device_plan.expected_observation: Window/title bar/dialog remain reachable without accumulated scaling drift, legitimate negative coordinates are supported, edits/last committed data survive and only one writer/teardown runs.
device_plan.evidence_to_retain: App commit, MSI hash, OS build, CPU, monitor topology, logical work areas/scale, before/after screenshots, process transitions, sanitized ordered flush/teardown events and recovered-ledger assertions.

device_plan.evidence_to_retain: Flatpak app/version/commit/hash/runtime and permissions, OS/compositor/backend, display topology/work areas/scale, screenshots, portal result if applicable, process transitions and sanitized write/recovery observations.

release_blockers: Code defect: resolve mutable ledger data to per-user durable app storage inside each shipped installation/sandbox; demonstrate standard-user save/reopen and retain existing data across updates.

Code defect: give cancellable Electron quit an explicit owner; prevent exit from outrunning persistence, cancel or join timed-out writers before disposal, handle flush rejection and serialize repeated quit without returning to a disposed session.
Code defect: validate stale restored bounds against current work areas and supported compositor behavior so the primary window remains usable after monitor removal.

Product decision and code/artifact correction: choose the Windows CPU support contract; reconcile the arm64 MSI declaration with the currently x64-only app and all SQLite/runtime dependencies. Native ARM64 cannot be claimed from the filename.
Product decision/evidence: identify old ledger locations, supported populated upgrade paths and retention/downgrade behavior; prove interrupted relocation preserves user data.

Hardware qualification: execute the physical monitor/docking tests on both desktops and native Windows ARM64 qualification if that support is retained; retain scoped results.
